items: suffix used to create primary imperfective intransitive verbs
suffix used to create derived perfective verbs, most of which are semelfactive

blocks.text: The primary (type-1) suffix is always unstressed. It forms verbs that are imperfective when unprefixed (perfective when prefixed, as usual), and are usually intransitive. The -н of the suffix tends to disappear in the past tense. Examples:

head: From
Word
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: (colloquial) to droop, to hang down, to dangle
to wave, to flap, to fling, to brandish
to grin, to smile, to smirk
to rock, to swing, to shake, to wobble; to dandle (once)
to crack, to burst, to pop
to reproach, to upbraid, to blame
to click (to make a clicking sound)
to exclaim, to gasp, to sigh
to stomp, to stamp one's foot

blocks.text: Pairs from Wiktionary's etymologies: each right-hand word is the left-hand word + -нуть, as Wiktionary records it.
